Three strategies will be evaluated for handling superseded documents. The first excludes superseded documents by default. The second retains them but applies a ranking penalty. The third selects behavior according to the temporal intent detected in the question.

Full exclusion improves answers about current rules but prevents historical questions from being answered. A fixed penalty reduces current-version errors without removing evidence, although an old version may still rank highly when it shares more terms with the query. The temporal strategy appears most appropriate: it prioritizes the current version for present-tense questions and retrieves earlier versions when the query contains a past date or asks for a comparison of changes.

The index must store validity period, supersession relation, and version. It will not rely only on `modifiedDateTime`, because a technical edit does not always change validity. Tomás will prepare a set of eighty current, historical, and comparative questions to measure precision and coverage.
